content.text: {"headline":"Approve P1: shift late-morning breaks by 45 minutes and switch on IVR callback, at no extra cost, for a predicted 91.0% service level from 10:00 to 12:00 against an 80% target.","why":"General calls are running 26% above forecast for the day so far, and service level fell to 44.1% at 09:45 with 6 abandons. Every call reason rose by a similar amount, and no marketing send, incident or absence explains it, so we can't tell how long it will last. Doing nothing (P0) is predicted to just clear target at 83.6%, with payments at 82.3%, which leaves little margin if the surge grows. P1 also costs nothing and lifts the window to 91.0% (payments 88.7%, general 94.2%). It cuts predicted abandons from 3.5% to 2.1% and needs no policy exceptions.","trade_offs":["Against P0 (no action, ₹0): same cost, but P0 runs close to target, especially on payments. P1 adds a buffer. The cost is that delayed breaks and callbacks shift some load later, so the rest-of-day forecast dips slightly from 92.6% to 92.3%.","Against P2 (chat deflection, ₹276): slightly better at 91.7% with 1.7% abandons, but it costs money for a small gain. It also targets balance enquiries when no single topic is driving the surge.","Against P3 (₹2,436) and P4 (₹5,760): overtime pushes the window to 95.9–96.3% with abandons of 1.0% or less, well above what the target needs. P4 is the hedge if the surge proves to be lasting.","Customer impact: callers on general from 10:00 and on payments from 11:00 will be offered a callback instead of waiting, and agents take their 11:00 breaks 45 minutes later."],"watch":"No escalation is needed. Because the cause is unknown, check general volume against forecast at around 10:30 and 11:00. If it keeps climbing or payments service level drops toward 80%, consider moving to the overtime options (P3, or P4 if the surge looks set to run past midday)."}
